Locked Workstation Recovery for Mint Studios Lab Windows 10 Desktop
Situation:

A lab Windows 10 desktop where the local Administrator password is unknown and not guessable. The technician has physical access, and the machine must stay assembled (no removing the drive — everything must be done in place).

Preparation:
Bootable USB/Installation Media:
Create a bootable USB drive with Windows 10 installation media using the Media Creation Tool from the official ??? website.
Ensure the USB drive is properly formatted and contains the necessary files.
Standard Recovery Procedure:

Power Off the Workstation:

Ensure the workstation is completely powered off.

Connect the Bootable USB Drive:

Insert the bootable USB drive into one of the available USB ports on the workstation.

Boot from USB Drive:

Power on the workstation.
Press the appropriate key to enter the BIOS/UEFI settings (commonly F2, F12, ESC, or DEL). The exact key depends on the system manufacturer.
In the BIOS/UEFI menu, navigate to the "Boot" or "Boot Order" section.
Set the USB drive as the primary boot device.
Save changes and exit the BIOS/UEFI menu. The system should now boot from the USB drive.

Windows Setup Screen:

On the Windows Setup screen, select the language preferences and click "Next."
Click on "Repair your computer" located at the bottom left of the window.

Troubleshoot Menu:

From the "Choose an option" screen, select "Troubleshoot."

Advanced Options:

From the "Troubleshoot" menu, select "Advanced options."

Command Prompt:

In the "Advanced options" menu, select "Command Prompt."

Rename the Existing SAM File:

In the Command Prompt window, type the following commands to rename the existing SAM file:
move C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM.bak

Press Enter after each command.

Reboot the System:

Close the Command Prompt window.
Select "Continue" to reboot the system.

Login to the Administrator Account:

After rebooting, the workstation should boot normally.
You will now be able to log in to the Administrator account without a password.

Set a New Password:

Once logged in, open the "Control Panel."
Navigate to "User Accounts" and then "Manage another account."
Select the Administrator account and choose "Change the password."
Set a new password and confirm it.

Verify and Document:

Ensure the new password works by logging out and logging back in with the new credentials.
Document the change and any steps taken for future reference.
Important Notes:
Ensure that all changes are logged and documented for accountability and future troubleshooting.
This procedure should only be performed by authorized personnel with proper training and authorization.

By following these steps precisely, you can regain access to the Administrator account on a locked Windows 10 desktop while keeping the machine assembled and the drive in place.
